nodes.title: Data I can trust. Daily US stock prices, returns and corporate actions, with index membership as it was on each date, including companies that later left.
No look-ahead, ever. Every model is fit only on data available at the time, and one shared check catches any step that peeks at the future.
One honest scoreboard. Every portfolio or strategy is scored out of sample on the same period, with the same trading costs, by after-cost Sharpe ratio (return per unit of risk) and realised variance.
Claims tested against chance. Every claim that a signal or model helps must pass a significance test before anything is built on it.
See it, don't just compute it. A browser app to explore the data and results, gaining views as each part lands.

A full build downloads every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time since 2000-01-03, with its prices, corporate actions and membership dates.

criteria: Given an empty store, when the owner runs the full build, then the store holds data for every stock in the primary source's membership history from 2000-01-03 to the latest close.

nodes.title: A daily update adds the latest trading day without rebuilding earlier days.

criteria: Given a store complete to day D-1, when the owner runs the update after day D's close, then day D is added and no stored value for an earlier day changes, unless a corporate action was announced; that case is listed in the run's report.

nodes.title: Cleaning removes or flags impossible values instead of filling them silently.

criteria: Given a raw row with a price ≤ 0, a high below the low, or negative volume, when cleaned, then the row is excluded from returns and listed in the validation report with its stock, date and reason.
Given a missing trading day for a stock that was a member that day, when cleaned, then the day stays missing (never filled with a zero return) and is counted in the report.

nodes.title: Returns are total returns: they include dividends and are corrected for splits.

criteria: Given a stock with a 2-for-1 split on date S and no price move, when daily returns are computed, then the return on S is 0%, not -50%.
Given a stock paying a dividend of 1% of its price on its ex-date, with a close-to-close price fall of 1%, when daily returns are computed, then the return on the ex-date is 0% (± 0.01%).

nodes.title: Every stock's closes are cross-checked against a second, independent source.

criteria: Given both sources cover a stock, when validated, then the report gives, per stock, the share of days whose split-adjusted closes agree within 0.5%, and the stock passes only if that share is ≥ 99%.
Given any day whose closes differ by more than 0.5%, when validated, then that stock, date and both values are listed in the report.

nodes.title: The owner's list of 10 delisted former S&P 500 members is checked on every full build.

criteria: Given the list of 10 stocks with their membership dates, when the full build finishes, then each one is present, its membership start and end dates match the list, and it has prices up to its last trading day; any mismatch fails the build's validation.

nodes.title: Data is stored once and reloaded without contacting any source.

criteria: Given a completed build, when research code loads data with no network connection, then it gets the same values the build stored.

nodes.title: The loader returns the data as it was known on a chosen date.

criteria: Given an as-of date T, when the owner loads the S&P 500 members, prices and returns, then only members on T are returned as current members, and no value dated after T is returned.

Given a stock that left the index on date E, when loading as of a date before E, then the stock is included; when loading as of a date after E, it is not a current member but its history up to E stays available.

nodes.title: The check reruns a step on data cut off at a date and confirms that outputs up to that date don't change.

criteria: Given a step and a cut-off date T, when checked, then every output dated on or before T is identical (to 1e-10 relative) whether the step saw data to T or to the latest close.

nodes.title: The check reports which outputs moved.

criteria: Given a step that uses one future value, when checked at any T before that value's date, then the check fails and names the first output date and column that changed.

nodes.title: Every step that fits, estimates or scores anything by date passes the check at 3 or more cut-off dates spread across the scoring period before it is used in a study.

criteria: Given a study run, when any step it uses has not passed the check at 3 or more cut-off dates, then the study refuses to run and names the step.

nodes.title: Coverage is summarised over time.

criteria: Given a built dataset, when the analysis runs, then it reports per year the number of index members, the number with prices on every trading day, and the number of missing member-days.

nodes.title: Return distributions and tails are summarised, using the data-analysis skill.

criteria: Given a built dataset, when the analysis runs, then it reports per year the mean, standard deviation, skew, excess kurtosis and 1st/99th percentiles of daily returns across members.
Given any daily return beyond ±50%, when the analysis runs, then it lists the stock, date and value for review.

nodes.title: Correlation structure is summarised.

criteria: Given a built dataset, when the analysis runs, then it reports the average pairwise correlation of daily returns among members per year.

nodes.title: The owner sees the index members on any chosen date.

criteria: Given a date from 2000-01-03 to the latest close, when chosen, then the app lists exactly the members the loader returns for that date.

nodes.title: The owner sees one stock's history.

criteria: Given a stock, when opened, then the app shows its daily closes and total returns over a chosen date range, with its membership periods marked.

nodes.title: The owner sees the latest validation report.

criteria: Given a completed build or update, when the owner opens the report view, then it shows the cross-check pass rate, the 10-name check result, and the listed problem rows.

nodes.title: The app shows progress of a running build or update without a page reload.

criteria: Given a build or update is running, when the owner has the app open, then its progress (stocks done out of total) updates at least every 5 seconds.

nodes.title: The app reads only stored data and stored results.

criteria: Given the network is down, when the owner opens any view, then it still shows the stored data.

nodes.title: Factors are the top k principal components of the members' standardised daily returns, fit on the walk-forward window only.

criteria: Given a refit date, when factors are fit, then they use only returns from the trailing 252 trading days, and the step passes the look-ahead check.

nodes.title: Residual returns are each stock's returns minus their fitted exposure to the k factors, with exposures from the same window.

criteria: Given a month after a refit, when residuals are computed for each day of that month, then they use the exposures fixed at the refit date.

nodes.title: The number of factors k is chosen from the window's eigenvalues, using only that window.

criteria: Given a refit date, when k is chosen, then k is the number of eigenvalues of the window's correlation matrix above the random-matrix noise edge (defined in COV-03), with at least 1.

nodes.title: Removing the factors lowers the correlation between stocks.

criteria: Given the scoring period, when residuals are computed, then the mean absolute pairwise correlation of residual returns is reported per year beside that of raw returns, and is lower in every year.

nodes.title: Stocks with short or broken histories are handled without biasing the panel.

criteria: Given a member with fewer than 200 of the 252 window days, when factors are fit, then it is left out of that refit and listed, and its gaps are never filled with zero returns.

nodes.title: The sample estimate is the plain sample covariance of the window's daily returns.

criteria: Given a refit date, when estimated, then it equals the sample covariance of the trailing 252 days' returns for the members kept by FACT-05.

nodes.title: The shrinkage estimate pulls the sample estimate toward a structured target, with a shrinkage intensity chosen from the window's data.

criteria: Given a refit date, when estimated, then the intensity is between 0 and 1, is reported, and is chosen using only the window.

nodes.title: The noise-filtered estimate replaces the correlation eigenvalues that fall inside the random-matrix noise band with their average.

criteria: Given a window of T days and N stocks, when estimated, then eigenvalues of the correlation matrix below the upper edge (1 + √(N/T))² of the noise distribution expected for pure noise of that shape are replaced by their average, the trace is kept, and the result is turned back into a covariance with the sample variances.

nodes.title: Every estimate is usable by the optimisers.

criteria: Given any estimate, when checked, then it is symmetric and positive definite (smallest eigenvalue > 0).

nodes.title: The three estimates are compared on how well they predict the next month's realised covariance, using the data-analysis skill.

criteria: Given the scoring period, when compared, then the report gives each estimate's monthly error against the next month's realised covariance, its eigenvalue spectrum, and its stability from month to month.

nodes.title: A shrinkage or noise-filtered estimate counts as better only if it lowers out-of-sample variance significantly against the sample estimate.

criteria: Given the minimum-variance portfolios built on each estimate (PORT-01) over the scoring period, when compared with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, then the result states, for shrinkage and for noise-filtered, whether realised variance is lower than with the sample estimate at 5% significance (after correcting for the two comparisons).

nodes.title: The minimum-variance portfolio has the lowest predicted variance allowed by the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given an estimate, when optimised, then no other weight vector meeting the portfolio rules has a lower predicted variance (to solver tolerance 1e-8).

nodes.title: The risk-parity portfolio gives every stock an equal share of predicted portfolio risk, within the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given an estimate, when built without hitting the 5% cap, then each stock's share of predicted risk is within 1% (relative) of 1/N.

nodes.title: The hierarchical risk-parity portfolio groups stocks by correlation into a tree and splits weight down the tree in inverse proportion to each branch's predicted risk.

criteria: Given an estimate, when built, then the stock order follows the tree's leaves, and at each split the two branches' weights are in inverse proportion to their predicted variances.

nodes.title: Every portfolio follows the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given any rebalance, when weights are produced, then they are ≥ 0, sum to 1 (± 1e-9), are ≤ 5% each, and cover only members on that date.

nodes.title: No portfolio uses return forecasts or any learned model.

criteria: Given the inputs to any classical portfolio, when inspected, then they are the covariance estimate and the member list only.

nodes.title: Every strategy is scored on the same dates with the same costs.

criteria: Given two strategies on the scoreboard, when compared, then both cover the same trading days and both are charged the same trading cost.

nodes.title: The scoreboard reports after-cost Sharpe ratio for each strategy.

criteria: Given a strategy's daily after-cost returns, when scored, then the annualised Sharpe ratio is the mean over standard deviation times √252, using after-cost returns in excess of zero.

nodes.title: The scoreboard reports realised variance for each strategy.

criteria: Given a strategy's daily after-cost returns, when scored, then annualised realised variance (daily variance × 252) is reported for the whole period and per year.

nodes.title: The scoreboard reports turnover and total cost paid.

criteria: Given a strategy, when scored, then average monthly turnover and total trading cost paid are reported.

nodes.title: Any claim that one strategy beats another is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given two strategies and a metric, when compared, then the result gives the test used, the p-value after correction for the number of comparisons made in that study, and whether it is significant at 5%.

nodes.title: "Beats the classical portfolios" has one fixed meaning.

criteria: Given a candidate strategy and the best S2 portfolio by after-cost Sharpe ratio over the same period, when compared, then the candidate beats it only if its after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher at 5% significance (SCORE-05) and its realised variance is ≤ 1.25 × that portfolio's.

nodes.title: The holdout is used once.

criteria: Given the holdout, when any S3, S4 or S5 study selects features, tunes or chooses a model, then no holdout day is used; when a final scoreboard run on the holdout is made, it is recorded with its date, and a second run on the same holdout for the same strategy is refused unless the owner marks it as a deliberate rerun, which the scoreboard then shows.

nodes.title: The app shows the scoreboard.

criteria: Given scored strategies, when the owner opens the scoreboard view, then it shows each strategy's after-cost Sharpe ratio, realised variance, turnover and cumulative after-cost return chart, filterable by stage.

nodes.title: Every candidate feature uses only past prices and volume.

criteria: Given a feature value for stock s on date t, when its inputs are traced, then they are prices and volume of stocks up to and including t only, and the feature passes the look-ahead check.

nodes.title: Targets are future residual returns over 1, 5 and 21 trading days.

criteria: Given date t and horizon h, when the target is built, then it is the sum of the stock's residual returns over days t+1 to t+h, and never includes day t's return.

nodes.title: A feature's information gain is the improvement in out-of-sample prediction of the target when a learned model is given the feature, compared with the same model without it.

criteria: Given a feature, a horizon and the walk-forward with a purge gap of at least h days, when tested, then the gain is reported per refit and on average.

nodes.title: A feature survives only if its information gain passes a test against chance with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given all candidate features and horizons tested, when assessed, then a feature survives only if its gain is significant at 5% after correction for the number of features × horizons tested, against a null where the feature carries no information.

nodes.title: Feature studies never use the holdout.

criteria: Given the holdout, when features are built, tested or chosen, then no holdout day is in any training or test set.

nodes.title: The app shows each feature's result.

criteria: Given a completed feature study, when the owner opens the feature view, then each feature shows its gain over time, its corrected p-value and whether it survived.

nodes.title: Forecast models are neural networks that read a sequence of past days of each stock's inputs.

criteria: Given a stock and an origin date t, when forecast, then the model's input is a window of that stock's surviving features (and past returns) for days up to and including t.

nodes.title: Forecasts cover future return and future volatility over 1, 5 and 21 trading days.

criteria: Given an origin date t, when forecast, then the model outputs the return and the realised volatility over days t+1 to t+h for each h in 1, 5, 21.

nodes.title: Models use only features that survived S3.

criteria: Given a forecast model, when its inputs are listed, then every feature on the list is marked as survived in the S3 study.

nodes.title: Training and testing follow the walk-forward with a purge gap of at least 21 trading days, and never use the holdout until the final run.

criteria: Given any training run, when its data is checked, then the last training target ends before the first test date, and no holdout day is used.

nodes.title: Return forecasts are compared with simple baselines.

criteria: Given the test periods, when scored, then the forecast's error and rank correlation with realised returns are reported beside a zero-return baseline and a trailing-mean baseline, and the forecast counts as better only if the difference is significant at 5% with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

nodes.title: Volatility forecasts are compared with simple baselines.

criteria: Given the test periods, when scored, then the forecast's error against realised volatility is reported beside a trailing-volatility baseline and an exponentially weighted volatility baseline, and the forecast counts as better only if the difference is significant at 5% with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

nodes.title: Training is reproducible.

criteria: Given the same data and the same random seed, when a model is trained twice, then its forecasts match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: The app shows forecasts against outcomes.

criteria: Given completed forecasts, when the owner opens the forecast view for a stock, then it shows forecast and realised return and volatility per horizon over time.

nodes.title: Portfolio weights use the forecasts made on the rebalance date.

criteria: Given a rebalance date t, when weights are set, then they use only forecasts with origin t and risk estimates from the walk-forward window.

nodes.title: Forecast-driven portfolios follow the portfolio rules and trading cost.

criteria: Given any rebalance, when weights are produced, then PORT-04 holds and the trading cost is charged.

nodes.title: Each forecast-driven portfolio is judged against the best S2 portfolio on the holdout.

criteria: Given the final holdout run, when compared by SCORE-06, then the scoreboard states "beats" or "does not beat" for each forecast-driven portfolio.

nodes.title: The owner adds or removes a strategy from the paper book.

criteria: Given a scored strategy, when the owner adds it, then its paper record starts on the next trading day with a stated starting value of 1,000,000 simulated dollars.

nodes.title: After each daily update, each paper strategy records its simulated trades and value.

criteria: Given a daily update for day D, when it completes, then each paper strategy records the trades it would make (on rebalance dates) at day D's close, pays the trading cost, and records its value at D.

nodes.title: Paper results are recorded forward only.

criteria: Given a past day's paper record, when any later run happens, then that record never changes.

nodes.title: The app shows the paper book.

criteria: Given paper strategies, when the owner opens the paper view, then each shows its value over time, its trades, and its after-cost Sharpe ratio and realised variance since it started.

nodes.title: The backtest environment replays history one trading day at a time and gives the agent only what was known that day.

criteria: Given day t, when the agent observes, then it sees members, prices, returns and features up to t only, and the environment passes the look-ahead check.

nodes.title: The agent's actions are portfolio weights that follow the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given any action, when applied, then the resulting weights satisfy PORT-04 and the trading cost is charged on their turnover.

nodes.title: The agent's reward is its after-cost return, with risk counted.

criteria: Given a step, when the reward is computed, then it is the after-cost portfolio return minus a variance penalty, whose weight is fixed before training and reported.

nodes.title: Agents are trained with proximal policy optimisation: each policy update is limited by clipping the ratio of new to old action probabilities.

criteria: Given a training update, when it is applied, then the clipping range (default 0.2) is recorded with the run.

nodes.title: Agents are trained and tuned on the walk-forward, never on the holdout.

criteria: Given any training or tuning run, when its data is checked, then no holdout day is used.

nodes.title: Each agent is judged against the best S2 portfolio on the holdout.

criteria: Given the final holdout run, when compared by SCORE-06, then the scoreboard states "beats" or "does not beat" for each agent.

nodes.title: Training is reproducible.

criteria: Given the same data and seed, when an agent is trained twice, then its holdout after-cost returns match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time since 2000-01-03, through the latest close.

criteria: Given any member-day in that range, when loaded, then all five values are present or the day is counted as missing in the validation report.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership with start and end dates, as it was on each date, including stocks later delisted, merged or removed.

criteria: Given any date since 2000-01-03, when the members are loaded, then the count is between 495 and 510.

nodes.title: Splits and dividends with their ex-dates for every stock in DATA-01.

criteria: Given a split or dividend in the primary source, when returns are computed, then it is applied on its ex-date (LOAD-04).

nodes.title: Delisted stocks keep their full history up to their last trading day, including the final price move.

criteria: Given a delisted stock, when loaded, then its last stored day is its last trading day.

nodes.title: A second, independent source of daily closes covers at least the stocks that are current members.

criteria: Given the current members, when cross-checked, then at least 95% of them are covered by the second source.

nodes.title: No real orders, real money or broker connection exist anywhere in the platform.

criteria: Checked by review: no code path places or sends an order to any outside party.

nodes.title: Data costs nothing beyond the owner's existing paid daily-data subscription and free sources.

criteria: Checked by listing every outside source the platform contacts; each is the existing subscription or free.

nodes.title: A full build from scratch takes ≤ 2 hours.

criteria: Timed on the owner's machine with a normal home connection.

nodes.title: A daily update takes ≤ 10 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the owner's machine.

nodes.title: Every study is reproducible from stored data.

criteria: Given the same stored data, settings and seeds, when a study is rerun, then its scoreboard numbers match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: The three estimates are compared on how well they predict the next month's realised covariance, using the data-analysis skill.

criteria: Given the scoring period, when compared, then the report gives each estimate's monthly error against the next month's realised covariance, its eigenvalue spectrum, and its stability from month to month.

nodes.title: A shrinkage or noise-filtered estimate counts as better only if it lowers out-of-sample variance significantly against the sample estimate.

criteria: Given the minimum-variance portfolios built on each estimate (PORT-01) over the scoring period, when compared with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, then the result states, for shrinkage and for noise-filtered, whether realised variance is lower than with the sample estimate at 5% significance (after correcting for the two comparisons).

nodes.title: The minimum-variance portfolio has the lowest predicted variance allowed by the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given an estimate, when optimised, then no other weight vector meeting the portfolio rules has a lower predicted variance (to solver tolerance 1e-8).

nodes.title: The risk-parity portfolio gives every stock an equal share of predicted portfolio risk, within the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given an estimate, when built without hitting the 5% cap, then each stock's share of predicted risk is within 1% (relative) of 1/N.

nodes.title: The hierarchical risk-parity portfolio groups stocks by correlation into a tree and splits weight down the tree in inverse proportion to each branch's predicted risk.

criteria: Given an estimate, when built, then the stock order follows the tree's leaves, and at each split the two branches' weights are in inverse proportion to their predicted variances.

nodes.title: Every portfolio follows the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given any rebalance, when weights are produced, then they are ≥ 0, sum to 1 (± 1e-9), are ≤ 5% each, and cover only members on that date.

nodes.title: No portfolio uses return forecasts or any learned model.

criteria: Given the inputs to any classical portfolio, when inspected, then they are the covariance estimate and the member list only.

nodes.title: Every strategy is scored on the same dates with the same costs.

criteria: Given two strategies on the scoreboard, when compared, then both cover the same trading days and both are charged the same trading cost.

nodes.title: The scoreboard reports after-cost Sharpe ratio for each strategy.

criteria: Given a strategy's daily after-cost returns, when scored, then the annualised Sharpe ratio is the mean over standard deviation times √252, using after-cost returns in excess of zero.

nodes.title: The scoreboard reports realised variance for each strategy.

criteria: Given a strategy's daily after-cost returns, when scored, then annualised realised variance (daily variance × 252) is reported for the whole period and per year.

nodes.title: The scoreboard reports turnover and total cost paid.

criteria: Given a strategy, when scored, then average monthly turnover and total trading cost paid are reported.

nodes.title: Any claim that one strategy beats another is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given two strategies and a metric, when compared, then the result gives the test used, the p-value after correction for the number of comparisons made in that study, and whether it is significant at 5%.

nodes.title: "Beats the classical portfolios" has one fixed meaning.

criteria: Given a candidate strategy and the best S2 portfolio by after-cost Sharpe ratio over the same period, when compared, then the candidate beats it only if its after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher at 5% significance (SCORE-05) and its realised variance is ≤ 1.25 × that portfolio's.

nodes.title: The holdout is used once.

criteria: Given the holdout, when any S3, S4 or S5 study selects features, tunes or chooses a model, then no holdout day is used; when a final scoreboard run on the holdout is made, it is recorded with its date, and a second run on the same holdout for the same strategy is refused unless the owner marks it as a deliberate rerun, which the scoreboard then shows.

nodes.title: The app shows the scoreboard.

criteria: Given scored strategies, when the owner opens the scoreboard view, then it shows each strategy's after-cost Sharpe ratio, realised variance, turnover and cumulative after-cost return chart, filterable by stage.

nodes.title: Every candidate feature uses only past prices and volume.

criteria: Given a feature value for stock s on date t, when its inputs are traced, then they are prices and volume of stocks up to and including t only, and the feature passes the look-ahead check.

nodes.title: Targets are future residual returns over 1, 5 and 21 trading days.

criteria: Given date t and horizon h, when the target is built, then it is the sum of the stock's residual returns over days t+1 to t+h, and never includes day t's return.

nodes.title: A feature's information gain is the improvement in out-of-sample prediction of the target when a learned model is given the feature, compared with the same model without it.

criteria: Given a feature, a horizon and the walk-forward with a purge gap of at least h days, when tested, then the gain is reported per refit and on average.

nodes.title: A feature survives only if its information gain passes a test against chance with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given all candidate features and horizons tested, when assessed, then a feature survives only if its gain is significant at 5% after correction for the number of features × horizons tested, against a null where the feature carries no information.

nodes.title: Feature studies never use the holdout.

criteria: Given the holdout, when features are built, tested or chosen, then no holdout day is in any training or test set.

nodes.title: The app shows each feature's result.

criteria: Given a completed feature study, when the owner opens the feature view, then each feature shows its gain over time, its corrected p-value and whether it survived.

nodes.title: Forecast models are neural networks that read a sequence of past days of each stock's inputs.

criteria: Given a stock and an origin date t, when forecast, then the model's input is a window of that stock's surviving features (and past returns) for days up to and including t.

nodes.title: Forecasts cover future return and future volatility over 1, 5 and 21 trading days.

criteria: Given an origin date t, when forecast, then the model outputs the return and the realised volatility over days t+1 to t+h for each h in 1, 5, 21.

nodes.title: Models use only features that survived S3.

criteria: Given a forecast model, when its inputs are listed, then every feature on the list is marked as survived in the S3 study.

nodes.title: Training and testing follow the walk-forward with a purge gap of at least 21 trading days, and never use the holdout until the final run.

criteria: Given any training run, when its data is checked, then the last training target ends before the first test date, and no holdout day is used.

nodes.title: Return forecasts are compared with simple baselines.

criteria: Given the test periods, when scored, then the forecast's error and rank correlation with realised returns are reported beside a zero-return baseline and a trailing-mean baseline, and the forecast counts as better only if the difference is significant at 5% with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

nodes.title: Volatility forecasts are compared with simple baselines.

criteria: Given the test periods, when scored, then the forecast's error against realised volatility is reported beside a trailing-volatility baseline and an exponentially weighted volatility baseline, and the forecast counts as better only if the difference is significant at 5% with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

nodes.title: Training is reproducible.

criteria: Given the same data and the same random seed, when a model is trained twice, then its forecasts match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: The app shows forecasts against outcomes.

criteria: Given completed forecasts, when the owner opens the forecast view for a stock, then it shows forecast and realised return and volatility per horizon over time.

nodes.title: Portfolio weights use the forecasts made on the rebalance date.

criteria: Given a rebalance date t, when weights are set, then they use only forecasts with origin t and risk estimates from the walk-forward window.

nodes.title: Forecast-driven portfolios follow the portfolio rules and trading cost.

criteria: Given any rebalance, when weights are produced, then PORT-04 holds and the trading cost is charged.

nodes.title: Each forecast-driven portfolio is judged against the best S2 portfolio on the holdout.

criteria: Given the final holdout run, when compared by SCORE-06, then the scoreboard states "beats" or "does not beat" for each forecast-driven portfolio.

nodes.title: The owner adds or removes a strategy from the paper book.

criteria: Given a scored strategy, when the owner adds it, then its paper record starts on the next trading day with a stated starting value of 1,000,000 simulated dollars.

nodes.title: After each daily update, each paper strategy records its simulated trades and value.

criteria: Given a daily update for day D, when it completes, then each paper strategy records the trades it would make (on rebalance dates) at day D's close, pays the trading cost, and records its value at D.

nodes.title: Paper results are recorded forward only.

criteria: Given a past day's paper record, when any later run happens, then that record never changes.

nodes.title: The app shows the paper book.

criteria: Given paper strategies, when the owner opens the paper view, then each shows its value over time, its trades, and its after-cost Sharpe ratio and realised variance since it started.

nodes.title: The backtest environment replays history one trading day at a time and gives the agent only what was known that day.

criteria: Given day t, when the agent observes, then it sees members, prices, returns and features up to t only, and the environment passes the look-ahead check.

nodes.title: The agent's actions are portfolio weights that follow the portfolio rules.

criteria: Given any action, when applied, then the resulting weights satisfy PORT-04 and the trading cost is charged on their turnover.

nodes.title: The agent's reward is its after-cost return, with risk counted.

criteria: Given a step, when the reward is computed, then it is the after-cost portfolio return minus a variance penalty, whose weight is fixed before training and reported.

nodes.title: Agents are trained with proximal policy optimisation: each policy update is limited by clipping the ratio of new to old action probabilities.

criteria: Given a training update, when it is applied, then the clipping range (default 0.2) is recorded with the run.

nodes.title: Agents are trained and tuned on the walk-forward, never on the holdout.

criteria: Given any training or tuning run, when its data is checked, then no holdout day is used.

nodes.title: Each agent is judged against the best S2 portfolio on the holdout.

criteria: Given the final holdout run, when compared by SCORE-06, then the scoreboard states "beats" or "does not beat" for each agent.

nodes.title: Training is reproducible.

criteria: Given the same data and seed, when an agent is trained twice, then its holdout after-cost returns match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time since 2000-01-03, through the latest close.

criteria: Given any member-day in that range, when loaded, then all five values are present or the day is counted as missing in the validation report.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership with start and end dates, as it was on each date, including stocks later delisted, merged or removed.

criteria: Given any date since 2000-01-03, when the members are loaded, then the count is between 495 and 510.

nodes.title: Splits and dividends with their ex-dates for every stock in DATA-01.

criteria: Given a split or dividend in the primary source, when returns are computed, then it is applied on its ex-date (LOAD-04).

nodes.title: Delisted stocks keep their full history up to their last trading day, including the final price move.

criteria: Given a delisted stock, when loaded, then its last stored day is its last trading day.

nodes.title: A second, independent source of daily closes covers at least the stocks that are current members.

criteria: Given the current members, when cross-checked, then at least 95% of them are covered by the second source.

nodes.title: No real orders, real money or broker connection exist anywhere in the platform.

criteria: Checked by review: no code path places or sends an order to any outside party.

nodes.title: Data costs nothing beyond the owner's existing paid daily-data subscription and free sources.

criteria: Checked by listing every outside source the platform contacts; each is the existing subscription or free.

nodes.title: A full build from scratch takes ≤ 2 hours.

criteria: Timed on the owner's machine with a normal home connection.

nodes.title: A daily update takes ≤ 10 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the owner's machine.

nodes.title: Every study is reproducible from stored data.

criteria: Given the same stored data, settings and seeds, when a study is rerun, then its scoreboard numbers match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: Data I can trust. Daily US stock prices, returns and corporate actions, with index membership as it was on each date, including companies that later left.
No look-ahead, ever. Every model is fit only on data available at the time, and one shared check catches any step that peeks at the future.
One honest scoreboard. Every portfolio or strategy is scored out of sample on the same period, with the same trading costs, by after-cost Sharpe ratio (return per unit of risk) and realised variance.
Claims tested against chance. Every claim that a signal or model helps must pass a significance test before anything is built on it.
See it, don't just compute it. A browser app to explore the data and results, gaining views as each part lands.

A full build downloads every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time since 2000-01-03, with its prices, corporate actions and membership dates.

criteria: Given an empty store, when the owner runs the full build, then the store holds data for every stock in the primary source's membership history from 2000-01-03 to the latest close.

nodes.title: A daily update adds the latest trading day without rebuilding earlier days.

criteria: Given a store complete to day D-1, when the owner runs the update after day D's close, then day D is added and no stored value for an earlier day changes, unless a corporate action was announced; that case is listed in the run's report.

nodes.title: Cleaning removes or flags impossible values instead of filling them silently.

criteria: Given a raw row with a price ≤ 0, a high below the low, or negative volume, when cleaned, then the row is excluded from returns and listed in the validation report with its stock, date and reason.
Given a missing trading day for a stock that was a member that day, when cleaned, then the day stays missing (never filled with a zero return) and is counted in the report.

nodes.title: Returns are total returns: they include dividends and are corrected for splits.

criteria: Given a stock with a 2-for-1 split on date S and no price move, when daily returns are computed, then the return on S is 0%, not -50%.
Given a stock paying a dividend of 1% of its price on its ex-date, with a close-to-close price fall of 1%, when daily returns are computed, then the return on the ex-date is 0% (± 0.01%).

nodes.title: Every stock's closes are cross-checked against a second, independent source.

criteria: Given both sources cover a stock, when validated, then the report gives, per stock, the share of days whose split-adjusted closes agree within 0.5%, and the stock passes only if that share is ≥ 99%.
Given any day whose closes differ by more than 0.5%, when validated, then that stock, date and both values are listed in the report.

nodes.title: The owner's list of 10 delisted former S&P 500 members is checked on every full build.

criteria: Given the list of 10 stocks with their membership dates, when the full build finishes, then each one is present, its membership start and end dates match the list, and it has prices up to its last trading day; any mismatch fails the build's validation.

nodes.title: Data is stored once and reloaded without contacting any source.

criteria: Given a completed build, when research code loads data with no network connection, then it gets the same values the build stored.

nodes.title: The loader returns the data as it was known on a chosen date.

criteria: Given an as-of date T, when the owner loads the S&P 500 members, prices and returns, then only members on T are returned as current members, and no value dated after T is returned.

Given a stock that left the index on date E, when loading as of a date before E, then the stock is included; when loading as of a date after E, it is not a current member but its history up to E stays available.

nodes.title: The check reruns a step on data cut off at a date and confirms that outputs up to that date don't change.

criteria: Given a step and a cut-off date T, when checked, then every output dated on or before T is identical (to 1e-10 relative) whether the step saw data to T or to the latest close.

nodes.title: The check reports which outputs moved.

criteria: Given a step that uses one future value, when checked at any T before that value's date, then the check fails and names the first output date and column that changed.

nodes.title: Every step that fits, estimates or scores anything by date passes the check at 3 or more cut-off dates spread across the scoring period before it is used in a study.

criteria: Given a study run, when any step it uses has not passed the check at 3 or more cut-off dates, then the study refuses to run and names the step.

nodes.title: Coverage is summarised over time.

criteria: Given a built dataset, when the analysis runs, then it reports per year the number of index members, the number with prices on every trading day, and the number of missing member-days.

nodes.title: Return distributions and tails are summarised, using the data-analysis skill.

criteria: Given a built dataset, when the analysis runs, then it reports per year the mean, standard deviation, skew, excess kurtosis and 1st/99th percentiles of daily returns across members.
Given any daily return beyond ±50%, when the analysis runs, then it lists the stock, date and value for review.

nodes.title: Correlation structure is summarised.

criteria: Given a built dataset, when the analysis runs, then it reports the average pairwise correlation of daily returns among members per year.

nodes.title: The owner sees the index members on any chosen date.

criteria: Given a date from 2000-01-03 to the latest close, when chosen, then the app lists exactly the members the loader returns for that date.

nodes.title: The owner sees one stock's history.

criteria: Given a stock, when opened, then the app shows its daily closes and total returns over a chosen date range, with its membership periods marked.

nodes.title: The owner sees the latest validation report.

criteria: Given a completed build or update, when the owner opens the report view, then it shows the cross-check pass rate, the 10-name check result, and the listed problem rows.

nodes.title: The app shows progress of a running build or update without a page reload.

criteria: Given a build or update is running, when the owner has the app open, then its progress (stocks done out of total) updates at least every 5 seconds.

nodes.title: The app reads only stored data and stored results.

criteria: Given the network is down, when the owner opens any view, then it still shows the stored data.

nodes.title: Factors are the top k principal components of the members' standardised daily returns, fit on the walk-forward window only.

criteria: Given a refit date, when factors are fit, then they use only returns from the trailing 252 trading days, and the step passes the look-ahead check.

nodes.title: Residual returns are each stock's returns minus their fitted exposure to the k factors, with exposures from the same window.

criteria: Given a month after a refit, when residuals are computed for each day of that month, then they use the exposures fixed at the refit date.

nodes.title: The number of factors k is chosen from the window's eigenvalues, using only that window.

criteria: Given a refit date, when k is chosen, then k is the number of eigenvalues of the window's correlation matrix above the random-matrix noise edge (defined in COV-03), with at least 1.

nodes.title: Removing the factors lowers the correlation between stocks.

criteria: Given the scoring period, when residuals are computed, then the mean absolute pairwise correlation of residual returns is reported per year beside that of raw returns, and is lower in every year.

nodes.title: Stocks with short or broken histories are handled without biasing the panel.

criteria: Given a member with fewer than 200 of the 252 window days, when factors are fit, then it is left out of that refit and listed, and its gaps are never filled with zero returns.

nodes.title: The sample estimate is the plain sample covariance of the window's daily returns.

criteria: Given a refit date, when estimated, then it equals the sample covariance of the trailing 252 days' returns for the members kept by FACT-05.

nodes.title: The shrinkage estimate pulls the sample estimate toward a structured target, with a shrinkage intensity chosen from the window's data.

criteria: Given a refit date, when estimated, then the intensity is between 0 and 1, is reported, and is chosen using only the window.

nodes.title: The noise-filtered estimate replaces the correlation eigenvalues that fall inside the random-matrix noise band with their average.

criteria: Given a window of T days and N stocks, when estimated, then eigenvalues of the correlation matrix below the upper edge (1 + √(N/T))² of the noise distribution expected for pure noise of that shape are replaced by their average, the trace is kept, and the result is turned back into a covariance with the sample variances.

criteria: Given the final holdout run, when compared by SCORE-06, then the scoreboard states "beats" or "does not beat" for each agent.

nodes.title: Training is reproducible.

criteria: Given the same data and seed, when an agent is trained twice, then its holdout after-cost returns match to 1e-6.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time since 2000-01-03, through the latest close.

criteria: Given any member-day in that range, when loaded, then all five values are present or the day is counted as missing in the validation report.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership with start and end dates, as it was on each date, including stocks later delisted, merged or removed.

criteria: Given any date since 2000-01-03, when the members are loaded, then the count is between 495 and 510.

nodes.title: Splits and dividends with their ex-dates for every stock in DATA-01.

criteria: Given a split or dividend in the primary source, when returns are computed, then it is applied on its ex-date (LOAD-04).

nodes.title: Delisted stocks keep their full history up to their last trading day, including the final price move.

criteria: Given a delisted stock, when loaded, then its last stored day is its last trading day.

nodes.title: A second, independent source of daily closes covers at least the stocks that are current members.

criteria: Given the current members, when cross-checked, then at least 95% of them are covered by the second source.

nodes.title: No real orders, real money or broker connection exist anywhere in the platform.

criteria: Checked by review: no code path places or sends an order to any outside party.

nodes.title: Data costs nothing beyond the owner's existing paid daily-data subscription and free sources.

criteria: Checked by listing every outside source the platform contacts; each is the existing subscription or free.

nodes.title: A full build from scratch takes ≤ 2 hours.

criteria: Timed on the owner's machine with a normal home connection.

nodes.title: A daily update takes ≤ 10 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the owner's machine.

nodes.title: Every study is reproducible from stored data.

criteria: Given the same stored data, settings and seeds, when a study is rerun, then its scoreboard numbers match to 1e-6.
